repository_purpose: macOS device-control substrate for agents, combining GUI automation, tmux control, job serving, and remote job submission.
findings: The repo is a deployment substrate for a Mac-centered topology, not a universal parent primitive.
Steer/Drive/Listen/Direct form a strong sidecar pattern for prod-device operation, but they require macOS permissions and machine topology the parent wrapper cannot assume globally.
The sentinel token pattern in Drive is a useful exact completion primitive for device-side terminal orchestration.

capability_rows.upstream_feature_name: Mac device sidecar for GUI, terminal, and remote job orchestration
capability_rows.validation_method: Validate host OS prerequisites, permission grants, remote job connectivity, and deterministic completion markers before treating a device sidecar as available.
capability_rows.blocker_or_dependency: Deployment-specific: requires macOS, Accessibility + Screen Recording + Full Disk Access permissions, tmux, SSH/remote connectivity, and the paired host topology.

trigger_logic: Only activate when a deployment explicitly names a Mac device sidecar.
actor_logic: The peer mesh host or deployment operator owns device admission and health checks.
validation_summary: Require permission and connectivity checks before any automation claim.
Keep the lane deployment-specific instead of quietly upgrading it to core.

overlaps: Pi-to-Pi tutorial context uses a Mac Mini + MacBook topology, but the peer mesh concept survives without this exact substrate.
Bowser covers browser use cases inside a broader validation workflow, while mac-mini-agent covers OS-level automation.
blockers: No blocker beyond deployment specificity; the lane simply should not be generalized to every parent installation.

source_refs.note: Documents Steer/Drive/Listen/Direct, sentinel markers, Mac permissions, and two-machine setup.

github_verification.note: GitHub due diligence pinned the cited upstream files to the verified commit snapshot used for this packet.
